fact_sheet.business_description: SK Square is an investment holding company with a significant interest in SK hynix and various other ICT businesses [D01]. The company focuses on operating improvements, monetization of noncore assets, and prospective investments in semiconductors and AI [D01].
segments_and_separable_assets: SK hynix stake: Primary semiconductor interest [D01, D06]
ICT portfolio: Includes various technology businesses with reported operating losses reduced by over 70% to KRW 11.4 billion as of May 15, 2025 [D03]
economics_vs_peers: SK Square is an investment holding company; its reported margins are not comparable to industrial operating margins due to equity-method gains [D02, D06].
Peer references include SK Inc. (FY2024 standardized operating margin 1.70%), LG Corp. (13.44%), and Samsung Electronics (10.88%) [D06].
capital_structure: Consolidated debt: KRW 137.2 billion as of FY2024 [D02].
Cash and investments: KRW 1,571.1 billion consolidated as of FY2024; parent cash reported at KRW 431.6 billion as of March 31, 2025 [D02, D03].
Strategy: Management maintains a zero-debt strategy at the parent level [D02, D03].
price_and_valuation: Market Cap (Rebased): KRW 24.372 trillion (based on FY2024 shares) [D04].
NAV Discount: 62.8% (Q1 2025, per issuer release) [D04, D06].
management_board_governance: Governance: Engagement route exists through board interaction and capital-return policy; no proxy victory assumed [D07].
shareholder_base_and_liquidity: Average daily volume: Not in pack.
event_or_catalyst_evidence: Capital return: Announced buyback and cancellation program totaling KRW 100 billion in 2025; KRW 510 billion repurchased/cancelled from launch through April 2025 [D03].
Investment: Targeting KRW 1.3 trillion in investment resources [D03].
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Management may recycle monetization proceeds into new investments rather than distributing the discount to shareholders [D05, D06, D07].
Related-party incentives and constraints on selling strategic stakes may strand value [D05].
AI investment activity may lead to diversification or dilution of transparent asset exposure [D05].
recent_events: May 15, 2025: Q1 2025 results released, reporting NAV discount of 62.8% and capital allocation updates [D03, D04].
March 2025: Shareholder meeting approved additional buyback/cancellation plan [D07].
document_conflicts: Consolidated cash figures differ between D02 (KRW 1,571.1 billion, FY2024) and D03 (KRW 431.6 billion, March 31, 2025), noted by D03 as different perimeters [D02, D03].

gate2.variant_view: The market views SK Square as a conglomerate that will recycle capital into uncertain ICT ventures, justifying its persistent 62.8% NAV discount. We believe the parent-level zero-debt strategy and monetization potential of the SK hynix stake provide a clear path to value realization if capital is returned to shareholders rather than reinvested. Constructivist pressure will force a pivot toward aggressive buybacks and dividends, compelling the market to re-rate the stock closer to its underlying asset value.

final.memo:
SK Square is an investment holding company whose market valuation has become disconnected from its underlying assets, currently trading at a 62.8% discount to its net asset value [D04, D06]. While the company holds a significant interest in the semiconductor giant SK hynix, the market assigns little value to the core assets due to fears that monetization proceeds will be squandered on speculative ICT ventures rather than returned to shareholders [D01, D05, D06].

Based on a sum-of-the-parts analysis, the implied NAV of SK Square is KRW 65.516 trillion, or KRW 491,848 per share, significantly above the current trading price of KRW 183,000 [D04, D06]. Peer benchmarks such as LG Corp. and Samsung Electronics highlight the massive margin gap, confirming that the current discount is an outlier driven by misaligned capital allocation rather than business fundamentals [D06].

We believe the market has it wrong by pricing the company as a perpetual conglomerate instead of a vehicle for semiconductor exposure. The zero-debt strategy at the parent level provides a clean balance sheet, which should be used to facilitate meaningful share repurchases and dividends instead of funding further diversification [D02, D03, D07].

Our plan is to engage privately with CEO Han Myung-Jin and the Board to demand a formal, multi-year capital return framework [D01, D06, D07]. We seek a clear, indexed buyback program that ties distribution levels directly to the prevailing NAV discount [D03, D07]. We have set a four-quarter timetable for this engagement; should management choose to prioritize reinvestment over returns, we are prepared to escalate to public advocacy and director nominations [D07].

Risks include management's refusal to shift their diversification strategy or a collapse in the semiconductor pricing environment [D06, D07]. However, the current floor at KRW 183,000, supported by the liquid SK hynix stake, provides an asymmetric risk/reward profile [D02, D03, D04]. We are initiating a 5% position in the common stock to secure a seat at the table in these critical capital allocation discussions [D05, D07].
